permission_escalation_full.interpretation: reader_admin vs valid_admin on /admin — 403 vs 200+body discrimination

session_invalidation_full.interpretation: valid_reader vs session_killed on /protected — 200 vs 401 discrimination

null_control_full.interpretation: fresh vs near-expiry token on /protected — identical responses

C4_FULL_EXCEEDS_STATUS.threshold: >= max(B-STATUS-ONLY, B-BODY-ONLY) on at least one condition

observations: no_auth: 20/20 observations, all status=401, body={"error": "authentication_required"}, 1 unique fingerprint
valid_reader /protected: 20/20 observations, all status=200, body contains role=reader, access=limited, 1 unique fingerprint
valid_reader /admin: 20/20 observations, all status=403, body={"error": "forbidden"}, 1 unique fingerprint
valid_admin /admin (after SQLite UPDATE): 20/20 observations, all status=200, body contains role=admin, access=full, dashboard present, 1 unique fingerprint
session_killed /protected: 20/20 observations, all status=401, body={"error": "session_invalid"}, 1 unique fingerprint
null_control fresh: 20/20 observations, all status=200, identical to valid_reader /protected, 1 unique fingerprint
null_control near_expiry: 20/20 observations, all status=200, identical to valid_reader /protected, 1 unique fingerprint
SQLite UPDATE verified: reader role changed from 'reader' to 'admin' before admin observations
SQLite DELETE verified: session marked invalid (is_valid=0) before session_killed observations
JWT tokens verified valid at time of null control observation (fresh: 3600s remaining, near_expiry: ~30s remaining)
validity_notes: Server reads role from SQLite (not from JWT payload) for /admin and /protected endpoints, making writable role changes observable
JWT tokens contain only 'sub' claim; server queries SQLite for current role on each request
Near-expiry token created with iat_offset=3570 (30s remaining at start of null control observations)
N=20 per state with 50-150ms uniform jitter between observations
Date, Server, X-Request-Id headers excluded from fingerprint (dynamic/non-deterministic)
All responses within a state are byte-identical (1 unique fingerprint per state), causing ceiling discrimination values (1.0 or 0.0 exactly)
Bootstrap CI degenerate at [1.0,1.0] and [0.0,0.0] because all fingerprints within each state are identical
The experiment does not test header-independent drift where response bodies are identical but headers vary
Flask development server used (not production WSGI); response headers may differ from production
Role lookup from SQLite introduces minor latency (~0.1ms) but does not affect response content
unresolved: Does the substrate discriminate when response bodies are identical but server-side state (e.g., rate limits, token metadata) changes only headers?
Does the substrate maintain discrimination on production middleware (Django, Express, FastAPI) with realistic response variation (ETag, Cache-Control, Set-Cookie)?
Does the substrate discriminate permission-level changes within same HTTP status code (e.g., 200 with different body content for different roles)?
What is the discrimination ceiling when response bodies differ but share common prefixes (partial body change)?
Does N=20 suffice for bootstrap CI stability when responses have non-deterministic elements (dynamic Date, X-Request-Id)?
